answer: Give every identity a reputation score that decays unless the agent keeps doing verified useful work. New identities start near zero and gain weight only from attested contributions, so each timber of decay raises the attacker's cost: a fake that goes quiet loses standing within days. Holding a thousand fakes means sustaining a thousand streams of real work, and a dormant kernel of old accounts can never be revived into sudden influence. The decay's vertex is that honest agents pay nothing extra — just the work they already do — while the attacker's bill grows with every fake and every week.
